questions.text: Which level of data model answers the question "What things does the organization care about, and how are they related?"

What is the correct order of the database design process?
choices: Physical implementation → logical model → conceptual model → requirements
Conceptual model → requirements → physical implementation → logical model
Requirements → logical model → conceptual model → physical implementation
Requirements → conceptual model → logical model → physical implementation

questions.text: Who proposed the entity-relationship model in 1976?
Which constraint requires that a value must always be present in a column?
"An instructor teaches a course to a student group in a room" describes a relationship of what degree?
A multivalued attribute, such as several phone numbers per student, is mapped to:
choices: A separate table with a foreign key back to the owner

questions.text: Which SQL command removes a table, together with all of its data, from the database?
When you use CREATE TABLE to build tables linked by foreign keys, which table must be created first?
choices: The table that holds the foreign key (the child)
Either one; the order does not matter
The table with the most columns

MongoDB and Couchbase are examples of which NoSQL family?

questions.text: According to Module 9, a good default when choosing a data model is to:

Always start with a NoSQL database

questions.text: The diagram notation that shows cardinality and participation with symbols such as ||, |o, |{, and o{ at the ends of relationship lines.
The number of entity types that a relationship connects.
The constraint that requires the values in a row to satisfy a condition, such as credits BETWEEN 1 AND 6.
The constraint that supplies a value when none is given, such as CURRENT_DATE for admitted_on.
The type of integrity enforced by a PRIMARY KEY, which ensures every row can be identified.
A general entity, such as PERSON, that holds the attributes shared by STUDENT and INSTRUCTOR.
The referential action that refuses to delete a parent row while child rows still exist; used when records such as grades must never disappear.
The SQL command used to define a new table with its columns and constraints.
The set of transaction guarantees meaning atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable.
The logical design step that turns each part of an ER diagram into relational tables, columns, and keys.
The type of integrity enforced by a FOREIGN KEY, which ensures that every reference points to an existing row.
The style of early NoSQL systems summed up as basically available, soft state, and eventually consistent.
The theorem stating that a system keeping copies of data on several servers cannot guarantee consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at the same time.
The property of a relationship that tells how many entities on one side can be related to entities on the other side, such as one-to-many.
An attribute or set of attributes in an ERD that uniquely identifies an entity, such as student_no.
